title: Finite presentation of a closed subspace and its structure quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Closed immersions are representable and become closed immersions of schemes on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Modules are on the small etale ringed sites, with quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$. A module is of finite type if etale locally finitely generated, and of finite presentation if etale locally it admits an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. A morphism is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; it is of finite presentation when additionally quasi-compact and quasi-separated (quasi-compact diagonal). The following are equivalent: $i$ is locally of finite presentation; $i$ is of finite presentation; $\mathcal I$ is of finite type; $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_X$-module. No Noetherian hypothesis, nor quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis on $X$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 084Q, lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, with automatic quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of a closed immersion; module quotient criterion from spaces-descent.tex Tag 0610, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module (forward), and sites-modules.tex Tag 082T, lemma-kernel-surjection-finite-onto-finite-presentation (converse).

proof.text: Every closed immersion of algebraic spaces is proper by lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper. In particular $i$ is quasi-compact and separated. Separatedness says that $\Delta_i$ is a closed immersion; applying the same lemma to $\Delta_i$ makes it quasi-compact. Thus $i$ is quasi-separated. By the finite-presentation convention in the statement, $i$ is therefore of finite presentation if and only if it is locally of finite presentation. This uses no quasi-compactness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 04XZ, lemma-closed-immersion-proper; Tag 084Q, lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, automatic finiteness conditions.

proof.text: Put $M=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. By lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules, $M$ and $\mathcal I$ are quasi-coherent and $\mathcal O_X\to M$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I$. For any affine etale chart $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, representability and def-weil-closed-immersion give $Z_U=Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ for an ideal $J\subset R$. The quotient and pullback identifications of lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence identify $M|_U$ with the structure quotient of this closed subscheme. The affine chart calculus computes its quotient map, kernel and cokernel on sections. Consequently $M(U)=R/J$ and $\mathcal I(U)=J$, with the map $R\to M(U)$ the quotient map, not a map to the conormal module $J/J^2$.

source.place: Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals, statement and proof; Tag 084Q, proof, restriction to scheme charts.

proof.text: For this affine closed immersion $i_U$, local finite presentation is equivalent to finite generation of $J$. Indeed, if $i_U$ is locally of finite presentation, lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation on its whole affine source and target makes $R\to R/J$ finitely presented. Apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg to the quotient surjection with zero polynomial variables: its kernel $J$ is finitely generated. Conversely, if $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, then $R/J=R[x_1,\ldots,x_0]/(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ is a finite algebra presentation. The affine pair $(Z_U,U)$ witnesses local finite presentation at every point by def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation. Ideal generation and module generation of $J$ both mean $J=\sum_{j=1}^m Ra_j$.

source.place: Tag 084Q, proof reducing to schemes; morphisms.tex Tag 01TV, lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation; algebra.tex Tag 00R2, lemma-finite-presentation-independent.

proof.text: By lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus, the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ (step 2) is of finite type if and only if $\mathcal I(U)=J$ is a finitely generated $R$-module for every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$. Suppose $i$ is locally of finite presentation and let $U\to X$ be such a chart. Choose any surjective etale scheme atlas $V_0\to X$ and put $V=U\sqcup V_0$, again a surjective etale scheme atlas. By lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test, with property locally of finite presentation and the identity chart of the scheme $Z\times_XV$ (a scheme by representability), $Z\times_XV\to V$ is locally of finite presentation. Its affine open $Z_U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ maps into the affine open $U\subseteq V$, so lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation makes $R\to R/J$ finitely presented, and lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg with zero variables makes $J$ finitely generated, as in step 3. Hence $\mathcal I$ is of finite type. Conversely, suppose $\mathcal I$ is of finite type. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V_0\to X$ and an affine open cover $V_0=\bigcup_kW_k$; then $V=\bigsqcup_kW_k\to X$ is a surjective etale atlas by a scheme whose components $W_k=\operatorname{Spec}R_k$ are affine etale charts. Each $J_k=\mathcal I(W_k)$ is finitely generated, so by step 3 the pair $(Z_{W_k},W_k)$ of affine opens witnesses finite presentation of $Z\times_XV\to V$ at every point of $Z_{W_k}$ in the sense of def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation. Since the $Z_{W_k}$ cover $Z\times_XV$, this morphism is locally of finite presentation, and lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test gives that $i$ is. This proves equivalence of local finite presentation of $i$ and finite type of $\mathcal I$.

source.place: Tag 084Q, lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, proof; Tag 0410, lemma-finite-presentation-local; spaces-properties.tex section-properties-modules.

proof.text: It remains to compare the two module conditions. On each affine etale chart, $M(U)=R/J$ by step 2. If $J$ is generated by $a_1,\ldots,a_m$, the sequence $R^m\to R\to R/J\to0$, with first map $(b_j)\mapsto\sum b_ja_j$, is exact, so $R/J$ is a finitely presented $R$-module. Conversely, if $R/J$ is a finitely presented $R$-module, apply lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel to $R\twoheadrightarrow R/J$; its source is generated by $1$, and its kernel is $J$. Thus $J$ is finitely generated. By lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus, applied to the quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal I$ and $M$ from step 2, these chartwise equivalences give $\mathcal I$ of finite type if and only if $M$ is of finite presentation. Combining steps 1 and 4 gives all four equivalent conditions.
